summary: On-prem Private: log forwarding to customer SIEM dropping events (Fluent Bit backlog/drops under load)
environment: prod (on-prem, air-gapped with controlled egress via SIEM relay)
description:
Issue summary
Customer reports that structured logs from Redwood Private (on-prem Kubernetes) are intermittently missing in their SIEM (Splunk via an on-prem relay). During peak inference load, the SIEM shows gaps in gateway/runtime logs (notably request lifecycle and error logs). Customer needs assurance of no event loss for audit/incident response requirements.

Impact
- Missing request/error audit trail in SIEM for portions of the day.
- Security/compliance team flagged as a go-live blocker unless event loss is addressed or bounded with documented mitigation.

Customer expectation
- At-least-once delivery to their SIEM relay, or clear operator guidance on how to configure buffering/retries to prevent drops.
- If drops can still occur, they want explicit metrics/alerts and a recommended sizing guide.

Environment
- Deployment mode: Redwood Private (on-prem)
- Cluster: Kubernetes 1.28, containerd
- Log pipeline: Fluent Bit DaemonSet -> customer relay (HTTPS) -> Splunk indexer
- Egress: restricted; only SIEM relay allowed
- Redwood components emitting logs: API gateway, serving runtime, control plane
- Observed load: ~220-320 RPS bursty, streaming enabled

Symptoms
- SIEM shows missing events for gateway access logs and runtime structured logs during bursts.
- Fluent Bit pod logs show intermittent output timeouts/retries.
- Fluent Bit internal metrics indicate dropped records when memory buffer fills.

Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Run synthetic load test (streaming chat completions) for ~20 minutes.
2) Observe Fluent Bit CPU/mem stable but SIEM count does not match expected event rate.
3) Review Fluent Bit logs: output errors and backpressure.

What we found / investigation notes
- Fluent Bit was configured with in-memory buffering only (no filesystem buffering) and a relatively small Mem_Buf_Limit.
- SIEM relay occasionally slowed to ~2-8s response time, causing backpressure on Fluent Bit output.
- Under backpressure, Fluent Bit started dropping events (confirmed by metric: fluentbit_output_dropped_records_total increasing).
- Additional contributing factor: high-volume, low-value logs (health checks / readiness probes) were being forwarded at the same priority as request logs.

Evidence (redacted)
- Fluent Bit output errors in flb logs (sanitized):
  - "[error] [http_client] response status=503"
  - "[ warn] [engine] failed to flush chunk ... retry in 10 seconds"
  - "[ warn] [output:http] could not flush records: timeout"
- Internal metrics snapshot (customer-provided):
  - fluentbit_output_errors_total: spikes during relay slowness
  - fluentbit_output_dropped_records_total: monotonically increasing during the same window

Workaround / resolution
We provided a supported configuration change to enable filesystem buffering + increase retry/backoff tolerance, and recommended filtering out low-value healthcheck logs to reduce volume.

1) Enable Fluent Bit filesystem buffering (prevents drops during transient SIEM slowness)
Customer applied the following changes to their Fluent Bit config (daemonset ConfigMap). NOTE: storage path must be writable on the node.

[Service]
    Flush        1
    Daemon       Off
    Log_Level    info
    Parsers_File parsers.conf

    # Enable local buffering
    storage.path              /var/log/flb-storage/
    storage.sync              normal
    storage.checksum          off
    storage.max_chunks_up     256


# Example: Tail input (container logs)
[Input]
    Name              tail
    Tag               kube.*
    Path              /var/log/containers/*.log
    DB                /var/log/flb_kube.db
    Mem_Buf_Limit     128MB
    Skip_Long_Lines   On
    Refresh_Interval  5
    storage.type      filesystem


# Example: HTTP output to customer relay
[Output]
    Name                  http
    Match                 kube.*
    Host                  <siem-relay.internal>
    Port                  443
    URI                   /services/collector/event
    Format                json
    tls                   On
    tls.verify            On

    # Retry/backoff
    Retry_Limit           False
    net.keepalive         On
    net.connect_timeout   10
    net.io_timeout        30


2) Filter out Kubernetes probe logs / reduce noise
Customer added a grep filter to exclude readiness/liveness probe traffic to reduce volume.

[Filter]
    Name   grep
    Match  kube.*
    Exclude log "kube-probe/"

We also recommended (optional) sampling INFO-level request logs if they continue to exceed relay throughput. Customer declined sampling for now due to audit requirements, but accepted filtering probe logs.

3) Validation
- After config change, customer repeated the same load test.
- fluentbit_output_dropped_records_total remained flat (no new drops) during relay slow periods.
- SIEM event counts matched expected within normal ingestion delay; missing windows no longer observed.

Customer confirmation
Customer confirmed on 2025-02-01 that event loss stopped and they can proceed with go-live, provided we document the buffering requirement as part of the on-prem min pack guidance.

Follow-ups
- Support to feed learnings into the Private observability minimum pack docs (on-prem defaults should include filesystem buffering and a baseline exclude-list for probes).
- Add an explicit 'log pipeline health' alert (drops/backlog) as part of the min pack; see related work in observability-pack PR-323.

2025-01-23 11:02 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Acknowledged. Asked customer to share: (1) Fluent Bit/Vector version, (2) output type (HTTP/syslog), (3) any buffering settings, (4) relay response codes/latency if available. Provided quick check: watch fluentbit_output_dropped_records_total and output retries.

2025-01-24 08:37 PT — Customer (Northbridge) — Shared Fluent Bit config. Mem_Buf_Limit=10MB, storage.type not set, Retry_Limit=10, output to HTTPS relay. Relay sometimes returns 503 during internal maintenance windows.

2025-01-24 09:10 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Root cause likely: in-memory buffer + finite retries + relay slowness => chunk drops. Proposed enabling filesystem buffering and infinite retries. Asked if node filesystem path is allowed under their security policy.

2025-01-24 13:46 PT — Kevin Osei (Eng, via Support) — Confirmed that for compliance use cases we should recommend filesystem buffering for on-prem. Also noted structured log fields are stable; ensure customer is on build that includes request_id/tenant/model/error_code (ref redwood/pr-28742).
2025-01-27 16:05 PT — Customer — Implemented filesystem buffering + increased Mem_Buf_Limit. Still seeing high volume; asked if we can help reduce low-value logs.

2025-01-27 16:22 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Suggested excluding kube-probe logs and optionally dropping GET /healthz routes at the collector. Provided grep filter snippet and guidance to keep ERROR logs unsampled.

2025-01-30 09:03 PT — Customer — Re-ran load test; no new drops observed. SIEM ingestion delay peaked at ~90s during relay slowness but events eventually arrived. Requested this be documented as the standard on-prem configuration.

2025-02-01 14:18 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Marking resolved. Added related links for min-pack logging pipeline health alerts and documentation updates. If drops recur, next step is sizing: disk buffer limit + relay capacity and/or dedicated log pipeline nodes.
